parked.originalReason: pauseWithdraw realigns phUSDDebt/stableDebt/promoDebt to the reduced amount at the CURRENT accumulators without paying out, so a user who emergency-exits during a pause forfeits ALL unclaimed accruals across all three streams. The forfeited stable/promo tokens stay in the contract and are ultimately swept to leftoverRecipient at finalizePromotion. This is explicitly documented as intentional at L523-525 (it fixes a latent V1/V2 underflow brick), so it is a deliberate trade-off — but the loser is the user and the beneficiary is the protocol/partner, and the pause windows in which it applies are created by routine flush operations. Routed for human adjudication: intended-but-user-adverse, and the alternative (pay out, or preserve the debt delta) was available.
parked.originalWhyLowConfidence: Documented intent + a real correctness motivation (underflow fix). Whether the forfeiture is acceptable is a design call, not a pattern verdict.
parked.deduplicatorConcurs: Yes — routing upheld. The pattern-matcher's framing ('a design call, not a pattern verdict') is exactly right.
parked.LEDGER_PRECEDENT_ADDED: STRONG, and it supports parking rather than promoting. The class is ledgered TWICE on sibling contracts and BOTH are dispositioned as accepted: L-06 (e7c217bc, src/Phlimbo.sol::pauseWithdraw, ACKNOWLEDGED, low) 'pauseWithdraw silently forfeits accrued rewards with no event and orphans per-share-accumulator residue'; V2-Q-01 (dfc30ff0, src/PhlimboV2.sol::pauseWithdraw, open, low) 'pauseWithdraw silent reward forfeiture + orphan residue (BLESSED BY KI-4)' with ledger description 'Blessed by KI-4 (forfeiture by design); QA only.' KI-4 is a registered known issue declaring the forfeiture intentional.
parked.consequence: A V3 instance would be a new fingerprint (different contract) but would land against an explicit KI + one acknowledged + one blessed precedent. Promoting it would re-litigate a settled design decision for the third time. Parked, not filed.
parked.reEmitTrigger: If KI-4's status ever flips, or if a human decides the V3 promo stream changes the calculus (the V1/V2 precedents predate the promo slot — PhlimboV3 forfeits a THIRD stream, promoDebt, that did not exist when KI-4 was blessed, and that stream's forfeited value flows to an owner-chosen leftoverRecipient rather than just sitting in the pool), re-emit as a Low.
parked.recommendation: Human adjudication only. Note the promo-stream angle above is the one genuinely NEW fact vs the blessed V1/V2 precedent, and no agent raised it.

parked.originalReason: withdrawAll sweeps the ENTIRE phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken balances including tokens backing live `unclaimable[token][user]` entries, leaving those claims unbacked — claimUnclaimable then reverts on transfer for the affected users, permanently unless the owner reimburses out of band. The docstring (L63-68) states this plainly as 'the accepted trade-off for keeping the emergency hatch unconditional and simple'. Under Law 3 this is a KNOWING owner action with an explicitly documented consequence, so it is close to trusted-and-suppressed rather than a footgun. Routed rather than dropped because the liability ledger and the swept balance are silently decoupled — no invariant or event warns the owner that live claims exist at sweep time.
parked.originalSuggestedMitigation: Track a `totalUnclaimable[token]` and either exclude it from the sweep or emit a warning event when sweeping over live claims — preserves the unconditional hatch while removing the silence.
parked.originalWhyLowConfidence: Explicitly documented and owner-knowing; likely suppressed at triage.
parked.SUPERSESSION: PARTIALLY PROMOTED. The pattern-matcher's instinct was correct on both counts and both halves are now resolved: (1) its BASE CASE is REFUTED — econ-scanner REFUT-08-R02 independently reached 'Law 3 obvious-consequence, suppress' with the NatSpec quoted verbatim, so 'likely suppressed at triage' was right; (2) the residual it correctly declined to drop — 'the liability ledger and the swept balance are silently decoupled' — is now DEDUP-08-09, corroborated by 3 further agents (ECON-08-003, F-08-02, LOCAL-105), and PATTERN-MR-002's suggestedMitigation (`totalUnclaimable[token]`) is the PRIMARY recommendation of that finding, proposed independently by 3 of the 4.
parked.whyStillParked: The entry is retained here because its base case is a live suppression decision a future run must not re-raise, and because the routing decision itself is the audit trail. Its promotable core has moved to DEDUP-08-09; nothing is lost either way.
parked.verdict: Routing VINDICATED. This is the clearest example this run of manual-review working as intended — a low-confidence route that neither dropped a real finding nor forced a weak one into the report.

parked.originalReason: `_tryTransfer` hands execution to an owner-onboarded partner token via a raw call inside batchClaim's loop. Checked and found largely mitigated: batchClaim is `nonReentrant`, and OZ ReentrancyGuard is CONTRACT-wide, so the whole sibling set (stake/withdraw/claim/collectReward) is locked for the duration. The debt is also aligned BEFORE the call (CEI-correct). Residual surface: a malicious promo token could re-enter the non-guarded owner functions (finalizePromotion, abortFlush) — but those are onlyOwner, so an attacker cannot reach them. Recorded as a checked-and-largely-refuted match; a malicious partner token remains an onboarding-diligence concern rather than a code defect.
parked.originalWhyLowConfidence: Guard coverage appears complete; no concrete reentrant path identified. Recorded for a human to confirm the owner-function surface.
parked.deduplicatorConcurs: Yes — and the pattern-matcher's specific request ('recorded for a human to confirm the OWNER-FUNCTION surface') is now the reason this entry matters more than its low confidence suggests. See MR-08-07, which is merged into it below.
parked.sastCorroboration: 5 aderyn potential-HIGH 'Reentrancy: State change after external call' hits land on exactly the owner-function surface PATTERN-MR-003 asked a human to confirm: src/PhlimboV3.sol L345, L347 (startPromotion), L370, L372 (topUpPromotion), L479 (finalizePromotion). DEDUPLICATOR VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE at bf42c12: `function startPromotion(address token, uint256 amount, uint256 duration) external onlyOwner whenNotPaused`, `function topUpPromotion(uint256 amount) external onlyOwner`, `function finalizePromotion(address leftoverRecipient) external onlyOwner` — ALL THREE carry onlyOwner and NONE carries nonReentrant. The pattern-matcher's claim that these are 'the non-guarded owner functions' is CONFIRMED, not assumed.
parked.WHY_THIS_IS_PARKED_AND_NOT_REMOVED: The task's SAST caveat covers '20 Aderyn potential-high reentrancy hits on MigratorV2V3.sol:161-194 — ALL inside nonReentrant migrate'. Only TEN of the 20 aderyn potential-highs are on MigratorV2V3 (SAST-006..015, removed as cluster R-01). These five are on PhlimboV3, on functions that are genuinely NOT guarded. Applying the caveat by its stated count (20) rather than its stated scope (MigratorV2V3.sol:161-194) would have silently removed five unguarded potential-highs on an in-scope contract. They are parked instead. This is a deliberate refusal to over-apply a caveat.
parked.assessmentOfActualRisk: LOW, and the parking is precautionary rather than alarmed. Reentering an onlyOwner function requires the promo token to call back DURING an owner transaction and the reentrant call to pass onlyOwner — i.e. the attacker must BE the owner, or the owner must have onboarded a malicious token AND the reentrancy must achieve something the owner could not do directly. Under Law 3 the owner is trusted non-malicious, so this reduces to: a malicious partner token, onboarded by a non-malicious owner, re-entering an owner-only function mid-call. code-scanner's R5 explicitly did NOT cover this surface (it walked the guard set reachable DURING A FLUSH; startPromotion/topUpPromotion are unreachable then). So this is an UNCOVERED surface with a plausible-but-thin threat model, not a refuted one.
parked.concreteQuestionForAHuman: Can a malicious promoToken, re-entering during startPromotion's `safeTransferFrom` (L345) or topUpPromotion's (L370), reach any state that makes the subsequent promoRewardBalance / promoRewardPerSecond assignment (L347/L372) inconsistent? Both functions assert an exact balance-delta (V3-L-04's `==` check at L352/L380), which likely blocks the interesting cases by reverting — but no agent verified that, and it is one probe to settle.
parked.recommendation: One Tier-2 probe or a human read of startPromotion/topUpPromotion's ordering. Cheap to close; currently the only in-scope potential-high surface this run leaves unadjudicated.

parked.originalReason: withdrawAll reads `promoToken` LIVE from PhlimboV3. After a rotation, the RETIRED promo token is no longer the live slot, so any balance of it stranded in the migrator can never be swept — withdrawAll only ever sees the current promo token (or none, once the slot is empty). Banked `unclaimable` entries for the retired token remain claimable by their users (which is fine), but any non-banked residue of a retired token is permanently stuck. Low impact; the residue should be zero in normal operation since deltas are forwarded or banked in full.
parked.originalWhyLowConfidence: No mechanism identified that leaves a non-banked residue; likely a theoretical gap only.
parked.SUPERSESSION: PROMOTED to DEDUP-08-10 (QA). story-faithfulness F-08-04 independently found the same gap and supplied the mechanism PATTERN-MR-004 explicitly could not: the BANKED case. If a user is banked in `unclaimable[tokenA][user]` during promo A and PhlimboV3 then rotates to promo B, tokenA is no longer the live slot — the owner cannot sweep it AND if that user is permanently blocked, the balance is stranded forever. PATTERN-MR-004 had assumed the banked case was 'fine'; it is fine for a user who CAN eventually claim, and stranded for one who cannot.
parked.whyStillParked: Routing decision preserved as the audit trail per instruction. The finding lives at DEDUP-08-10.
parked.verdict: Routing correct on the evidence available to the pattern-matcher; the low-confidence note was honest and the gap it left open is exactly the one another agent filled. Convergence, not correction.

parked.SUPPRESSION_STATUS: HOLDS — the trigger as written has NOT fired. econ-scanner: 'The literal precondition of the DEDUP-04 suppression (desiredAPYBps == 0) still HOLDS at the deploy instant for V3, so the trigger as written has not fired and I am not re-emitting the High unilaterally.' The deduplicator does NOT re-emit it either.
parked.WHY_THIS_IS_PARKED_ANYWAY: econ-scanner's explicit instruction: 'Surface to triage as a live re-emit CANDIDATE, not a silent re-suppression.' The suppression's RATIONALE is materially weaker for V3 than the V1-era known-issue claims, and re-suppressing without surfacing that would be exactly the silent-drop Law 1 forbids. The ledger's own suppression note commits to this channel ('Kept in this VISIBLE channel per Law 1 with the explicit re-emit trigger').
parked.shippedDefault: desiredAPYBps == 0 at deploy, BY CONSTRUCTION: PhlimboV3's constructor (L200-216) never assigns desiredAPYBps, so it is zero-initialised, and _updatePhUSDEmissionRate then yields phUSDPerSecond == 0, gating the mint at L736. Reaching a non-zero value needs two owner setDesiredAPY calls within 100 blocks (two-step preview/commit, L223-239). No deployment script exists in the repo (no script/ dir) and no story sets a V3 APY.
evidenceAgainstSuppression: THE V1-ERA-KI HAZARD, REALISED: the 'APY should be 0 by default' assertion cited for KI-10 is at test/PhlimboEMATest.t.sol:1543, whose fixture is `PhlimboEA public phlimbo; phlimbo = new PhlimboEA(...)` (L24, L44) — it is a V1 TEST. It is evidence about V1, NOT V3. This is precisely the V1-era-KI-suppressing-a-V3-finding hazard.

SolvencyDetermination.md — the V3 design doc shipped AT THIS COMMIT — SPECIFIES the non-zero-APY mint path as a SUPPORTED operating mode, not a disabled one. §2 (L32-44): pending phUSD is 'minted on demand at settlement — there is no pre-funded pool and therefore no balance-style insolvency', gives the live emission formula 'totalStaked * desiredAPYBps / 10000 / SECONDS_PER_YEAR', and reduces phUSD solvency to a single condition: holding an active mint privilege. The V3 spec treats unbacked, APY-driven phUSD minting as intended and solvent BY DESIGN.

MigratorV2V3's own NatSpec (L43) frames APY->0 as a WIND-DOWN action for the venue being RETIRED: 'wind V2 down (owner sets APY->0, stop feeding collectReward), then run a second migrator pass'. This implies the LIVE venue carries a non-zero APY and that V3, as V2's successor, inherits that role.

test/MigratorV2V3Test.t.sol:103-105 seeds the migration's production-representative baseline with `phlimboV2.setDesiredAPY(500)` commented 'Non-zero V2 phUSD APY so phUSD rewards accrue' — the modelled live V2 runs 5% APY, and the entire point of MigratorV2V3 is to move that user base into V3.
parked.assessment: PRESERVED VERBATIM FROM econ-scanner: 'KI-10's stronger claim — that zero-APY is the shipped default AND EXPECTED — is only supported by V1 evidence, and the V3 artefacts point the other way: the V3 design doc specifies the APY-driven mint as a supported mode with no cap and no backing, and the migration narrative reads as V3 taking over a venue that currently runs 500 bps. Suppression now rests entirely on an operational choice (owner never commits a non-zero APY) that no artefact in the repo actually commits to.'
parked.DEDUPLICATOR_ADDS: This is not an isolated question — it is the THIRD place this run where the zero-APY assumption is load-bearing, and the connections were not visible to any single agent: (1) DEDUP-08-06's phUSD over-emission leg is 'APY-bounded' per the profiler, i.e. immunised at zero-APY and live at non-zero; (2) ledger V2-M-03 (wont-fix, medium) carries the IDENTICAL conditional in its own description — 'Zero-APY (KI-10) immunizes -> Medium; RE-CLASSIFY HIGH if a non-zero-APY config ships'; (3) DEDUP-04 itself. A single owner answer therefore re-weighs at least three findings across two contracts and two runs. That makes it the highest-leverage open question of this audit, above even DEDUP-08-05's token decimals.
recommendedAction: ASK THE OWNER DIRECTLY: is a non-zero desiredAPYBps intended for V3 post-migration? If YES, DEDUP-04 reclassifies HIGH immediately per its own trigger, V2-M-03 reclassifies HIGH per its own note, and DEDUP-08-06's phUSD leg becomes live.

RE-EXTRACT the 10 cached known-issues (dated 2026-01-15, V1-era) against V2/V3 before ANY further KI-based suppression in this project. econ-scanner recommends this and the deduplicator strongly concurs — KI-10 has now been shown to rest on a V1 test fixture while being applied to V3.
Do NOT silently re-suppress DEDUP-04 on the strength of KI-10 without reading the above.

parked.reason: TWO low-value observations on abortFlush, parked together because they share a function and an observability theme, and because abortFlush is where DEDUP-08-01's non-determinism lives — a reader looking at that finding should see these. (1) LOCAL-006 (profiler, local-info): abortFlush does not reset flushCursor. BENIGN AT PRESENT because beginFlush unconditionally sets flushCursor = 0 (L416), so a stale cursor cannot leak into the next flush. Recorded as a LATENT COUPLING: the safety of abortFlush depends ENTIRELY on beginFlush's reset, and finalizePromotion's `flushCursor == _stakers.length()` guard would be TRIVIALLY SATISFIABLE by a stale cursor if that reset were ever removed. (2) SAST-082 (aderyn, 'State Change Without Event'): abortFlush mutates promoPhase and emits nothing.
parked.deduplicatorVerification: Read src/PhlimboV3.sol:498-501 at bf42c12. Confirmed abortFlush is THREE lines: `require(promoPhase == PromoPhase.Flushing, ...); promoPhase = PromoPhase.Active;` and nothing else. It calls no _updatePool, resets no cursor, emits no event. Both observations are accurate.
parked.whyParkedNotFiled: (1) is explicitly benign today and is defence-in-depth. (2) is event noise of the class already ledgered three times (L-01, L-04, V2-L-04, V2-Q-02) and sits in the 'missing event emissions = QA at best' filter. Neither clears the bar alone.
parked.whyNotSimplyRemoved: abortFlush is doing more nothing than it should. It is the exit path where DEDUP-08-01's whole-window promo swing is decided, where LOCAL-006's cursor is left stale, and where no event records that a rotation was abandoned. The one-line fix recommended by three agents for DEDUP-08-01 is to make abortFlush call _updatePool — i.e. abortFlush is already slated for a change. If it is touched, resetting flushCursor and emitting an event are near-free additions. Parked so that they are on the table at the same time rather than discovered a run later.
parked.recommendation: If DEDUP-08-01's abortFlush fix is implemented, fold in `flushCursor = 0` and a `FlushAborted` event. Otherwise no action.
